taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: stems slender, 1-4(-7) dm. high; P. Tolmiei (p. 738), the Mount Rainier plant: 0.5-1.5 dm.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: stems 1-4(-7) dm. high.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 732, Penstemon: perennial herbs or shrubs.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: the herbage essentially glabrous: a herb.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the flowering stems die back each winter.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: the basal rosette feebly-developed; P. Tolmiei (p. 738): basal rosette well-developed.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 732, Penstemon: leaves opposite.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: the basal lanceolate to oblanceolate, 2-6 cm. long including the short slender petiole.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: leaves 4 mm to 1.5 cm wide, as in the photos.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the basal leaves' short slender petiole 5 mm to 1.5 cm (Abrams 1951 p. 738); the upper leaves sessile (p. 732), so set from 0.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: the basal lanceolate to oblanceolate, the cauline broadly oblong to narrowly lanceolate.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 735, Penstemon subsection Proceri: leaves very entire (key).

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: the herbage essentially glabrous.

traits.inflorescence.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: thyrsus strict, of 1-6 dense clusters, the lower often well spaced: drawn as a raceme of crowded flowers near the stem's top.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 735, Penstemon subsection Proceri: corolla 6-10 mm. long, more or less declined (key); P. Tolmiei (p. 738): 9-11 mm.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 732, Penstemon: corolla tubular, the throat often ampliate.

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: calyx-lobes 3-6 mm. long.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon procerus: corolla blue-purple; P. Tolmiei: deep blue-purple or sometimes pale yellow; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951) p. 738, Penstemon Tolmiei (now P. procerus var. tolmiei, the variety at Mount Rainier): June-Aug.; Abrams gives May-Aug. for P. procerus at lower elevations.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: capsules ripe August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low clump of slender stems with pairs of narrow, smooth, deep green leaves, ending in one to several dense whorls of small blue-purple tubular flowers. The basal leaves' petiole share is set by hand from the leaf and petiole lengths the traits give, as no rule sets a rosette leaf's.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for small-flowered penstemon from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.2 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
